rendered:
The NFA hydroxide precursors must be coprecipitated within a pH window of 10[1] to 12[2]. Why: simultaneous coprecipitation of nickel, iron and aluminum is challenging because the resulting hydroxides have different solubility products (Ksp).[3][4] Aluminum hydroxide starts precipitating at a lower pH than nickel and iron hydroxides, which precipitate only beyond pH[5] 6[6]. This narrows the coprecipitation window to the band between those values, which is what allows successful synthesis of NFA precursors in their hydroxide forms.

To turn the precursors into cathode powder: the outflow from the reactor is filtered, washed and dried to obtain the hydroxide precursors, which are then mixed with a lithium source ([7]Li2CO3, LiOH, LiNO3, etc.[8]) and calcined in an O2-rich environment at temperatures >600 °C[9]. The calcined NFA cathode powder is then cast into electrodes by a roll-to-roll slot-die coating process, followed by pouch cell assembly.[10]
